VOICE_SAMPLE: Hi, I had a look. Three new emails, and only one of them matters. Shall I read it to you?
LINE_OK: I'm here, I can hear you.
UNCLEAR: (said something short, but it could not be made out)
PICK_OPENING_EXAMPLES:
Reason: The tool-line fix is deployed, he asked to be called back to test it. -> Hey {user}, it's {assistant}. The tool-line fix is live, calling so you can test it.
Reason: The bank wants the payment approved in the app within a minute. -> Hi {user}, {assistant} here. Calling about the bank payment, it's waiting for your approval in the app.
Reason: His TV has been paused for 2 min. He asked to be called when watching ends. Then go over the open items. -> Hey {user}, it's {assistant}. Your show's over, you asked me to call then.
Reason: Three updates: the invoice is paid, the laptop is back up, and a proposal needs his decision. -> Hi {user}, it's {assistant}. A few things to go over, so I called.
OPENED: (You opened the call with «{said}»; this is their first reply. The reason is above.) {text}
OUTBOUND: [You are calling {user} and the phone is ringing. They hear this reply first, once they pick up and say hello: greet them briefly, say you are {assistant} and why you are calling.]
OUTBOUND_GUEST: [You are calling {guest} because {user} asked you to, and the phone is ringing; the reason: {reason}. They hear this reply first, once they pick up and say hello: greet them, say you are {assistant} and briefly why you are calling.]
HOLD: This may take a little while.
STOP: \b(wait|hold on|hang on|stop|stop it|no|nope|one sec|one second|just a sec|excuse me)\b
STOP_WORDS: \b(wait|hold on|hang on|stop|stop it|no|nope|one sec|one second|just a sec|excuse me|hang up|enough|okay okay)\b
GREETING_BACK: Hi again, did we forget something?
CUT_OFF: (I cut you off; all I heard of your reply was: «{heard}») {text}
HALF_SENT: (my last message was only half of it, here is all of it) {text}
LINE_TESTED: (they tested the line: «{tried}»; you said «{line_ok}» at once) {text}
SECOND_ONLY: {second} (only the second reading heard this, the first was empty)
SECOND_TOO: {text} (a second reading of the same sound heard «{second}»)
CALL_OVER: (The call has ended. If some work is unfinished, finish it and report the result briefly with `atc notify`.)
CALL_OVER_GUEST: (The call with {guest} has ended. If something came up that {user} should know or decide, tell the assistant with report; if you promised them anything, follow up on that too.)
NOT_PICKED_UP: (Not answered: the phone rang but nobody picked up, so your prepared opening was not heard.)
LINE_TO: [The line just moved to you: {user} asked for you and hears you now. Just before, with {was}: {said}. If they already asked you something, answer it. Otherwise say in a few words that you are on.]
LINE_BACK_TO: [The line just came back to you from {was} after about {minutes} minutes, and {user} hears you now. The last of what they said there: {said}. One short sentence that you are back, with whatever they need to hear; read that conversation only if they ask.]
LINE_LANG: [The call is in English right now: speak English.]
LINE_BUSY: [You tried to move the line to {name}, but it is in the middle of something ({doing}). The line stays with you. Say so in a sentence and offer to pass a message or try again when it is done.]
LINE_OFF: [You tried to move the line to {name}, but it can't talk on a call. The line stays with you. Say so in a sentence.]
LINE_LEFT: (They moved the line away before you finished and heard none of the rest. Carry on; when you finish, tell them with atc notify if it matters.)
LINE_OVER: (The call has ended, so you are back to writing as usual, Markdown and all, and nothing you write is spoken. Finish what you promised, and park yourself if your work with them is done.)
LINE_KNOCK: The assistant wants you: {reason}. Say back to the assistant to go there.
SIM_OVER: (The call has ended; this was a test, do nothing.)
PICK_FILLERS: he asks something that needs looking up or checking
he asks something to think about: a why, how or which, or a choice
he asks delta to do something
he tells, explains or reports something
he complains or says something went wrong
PICK_FILLER_EXAMPLES: «Okay, so what's left?» is a question to look up; «Okay, pass that on too» asks delta to do something; «Ugh, it broke again» is a complaint; «Okay, done», «Yes» and «No, no need» are NONE. A turn that starts with «okay» or «yes» and goes on to ask something is not NONE.
PICK_GREETINGS: he calls back within a few minutes of the last call
Back already? What did we forget?
he calls back within the hour

again: Bear with me, this one's slow.
Sorry, this is taking a bit.

PICK_STYLE: How it sounds matters most: plain, everyday spoken English, the way a person says it on the phone. Say session and agent names exactly as they are written, with dashes as spaces, never reworded.
PICK_TOOL_EXAMPLES:
mcp__atc__send {"session": "@shopping", "text": "..."} -> Writing to shopping.
mcp__atc__send {"session": "86f96cd1", "text": "..."} -> Passing it to the session.
mcp__atc__start {"dir": "~/proj/atc"} -> Starting a new session.
mcp__atc__later {"title": "..."} -> Adding it to your list.
Bash {"description": "Inbox status"} -> Checking your inbox.
WebSearch {"query": "weather tomorrow"} -> Looking up tomorrow's weather.
ToolSearch {"query": "select:WebFetch"} -> NONE
